requirements.text: Every advertised feature exists and works end to end.
Every advertised action has a discoverable entry point.
Every entry point produces a truthful, verifiable result.
Every workflow has loading, success, empty, error, cancellation, and recovery states.
No placeholder, dead control, demonstration-only response, fabricated data, or hidden developer prerequisite ships.
Features work with a new user account and with existing user data.
A customer installs from one current, signed release artifact.
A fresh machine needs no repository, compiler, package manager, terminal command, developer account, or undocumented runtime.
Required models, voices, assets, helpers, schemas, migrations, and supported local services are packaged or installed by the signed setup flow.
First launch detects and repairs incomplete setup.
Installation, update, repair, uninstall, and reinstall are tested.
The running binary is proven to match the current source commit and package hash.
The app explains what it needs, why it needs it, and what remains usable without it.
Permission requests occur in context.
Every Open Settings action opens the exact relevant operating-system destination when the platform permits deep linking.
When direct navigation is unavailable, the app provides accurate, version-specific steps and confirms completion after the user returns.
Denial, revocation, restriction, and later approval all recover without reinstalling.
Setup can be resumed safely after interruption.
A setup guide exists inside the product and is also available outside it.
Every capability that can depend on hardware, an account, a provider, a network, or external data has a working built-in local fallback that lets the user understand and use the product immediately.
Every such capability has a guided real connection path that authenticates, validates, exercises, and proves the supported external service or hardware.
Fallbacks are clearly identified and never masquerade as live data, live hardware, sent communication, real analytics, or completed external actions.
The information architecture maps every product promise to a visible user journey.
Labels, instructions, and outcomes use consistent language.
Navigation never strands the user.
Destructive or consequential actions clearly identify their target and result.
Immediate actions acknowledge immediately; longer work shows progress, supports cancellation where safe, and finishes with a useful result or actionable recovery.
Voice actions, where offered, visibly acknowledge capture and mode changes; recording or note-taking visibly shows its active state and produces an end summary.
No workflow depends on the user knowing an undocumented phrase or command.

No supported window size, display scale, text size, language, orientation, or accessibility setting causes overlap, clipping, illegible text, hidden controls, unreachable content, or input obstruction.
Desktop products pass minimum window, maximum window, full-screen, multi-display, scaled-display, and high-DPI tests.
Windows products pass 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, and 200% display scaling where supported.
Apple products pass supported Dynamic Type and accessibility settings.
Keyboard navigation, focus order, screen-reader labels, contrast, reduced motion, and non-pointer operation are complete.
Layout tests include long localized strings and realistic maximum-content states.
Repeated launch, force quit, crash recovery, sleep/wake, restart, user switching, network loss, provider outage, device loss, and interrupted work do not corrupt state.
Offline behavior is deterministic and honestly represented.
Failed jobs can be retried without duplication or data loss.
Migrations preserve legitimate user data.
Repair and reset operations identify exactly what they change.
Support diagnostics are user-accessible, privacy-safe, and actionable.
Direct mode changes and local interface state changes acknowledge immediately.
Where voice input is offered, activation, listening state, and cancellation give immediate visible feedback.
The interface does not freeze, flash, jump unexpectedly, or appear dead during supported work.
App-specific measurable launch, interaction, processing, memory, storage, and energy thresholds are defined and met.
Performance evidence is collected on the minimum supported hardware, not only a development machine.

Distributed packages contain no source code, source maps, debug symbols, credentials, signing material, private datasets, internal prompts, test fixtures containing private data, or development tooling.
Production binaries are signed, hardened, stripped, integrity-checked, and protected against casual extraction and tampering.
Proprietary logic uses compiled modules, obfuscation, encrypted assets, and server-held components where that does not violate required local operation.
Licensing resists copying and redistribution while preserving legitimate install, reinstall, update, and recovery.
Updates require authenticated, signed packages and resist rollback and spoofing.
Secrets remain in approved secure storage and never appear in logs, packages, crash reports, or client-visible diagnostics.
Dependencies pass vulnerability, license, provenance, supply-chain, malware, and secret scans.
Every platform receives package inspection, extraction, tampering, entitlement-bypass, update-spoofing, and clean-room replication tests.
A recipient cannot reconstruct source, extract protected assets, retrieve secrets, bypass product controls, or clone a functional product from the shipped artifact.
Real-world claims are backed by real sources.
Synthetic or demonstration data is unmistakably labeled and isolated from live results.
Empty states remain honest.
The shipped package contains no developer, employee, test-user, or previous customer's private data.
Calculations expose their inputs and can be reproduced.
Actions claimed as sent, published, recorded, connected, controlled, or completed have receipts from the responsible system.
A first-run guide, feature guide, permission guide, integration guide, recovery guide, and uninstall guide exist.
Instructions match the current release and each supported operating-system version.
Help is reachable from the relevant feature.
Error messages explain what happened, what was preserved, and the next recovery action.
The user can export a privacy-safe diagnostic bundle without development tools.
Tests attempt to disprove completion, not merely confirm the happy path.
Every requirement includes success, boundary, denial, interruption, repetition, malformed-input, stale-state, and recovery cases where applicable.
Clean-machine tests use machines with no prior installation of the product.
Existing-machine tests include supported prior releases and realistic user data.
Release testing uses the distributed package, never only a development run.
The final verdict is derived from evidence, not a subjective sign-off.
